chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Yunus ibn Hisham from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would often spit on the Day of Ashura into the mouths of the nursing children from the offspring of Fatimah (peace be upon her) from his saliva, and he would say, 'Do not feed them anything until night,' and they would derive benefit from the saliva of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
He said, 'And the beasts would fast on the Day of Ashura during the time of David (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ: The Day of Ashura (10th of Muharram)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet spitting into the mouths of infants on Ashura?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s specific devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt by transferring barakah through his saliva to the nursing infants of Fatimah (peace be upon her) on Ashura, a day of fasting and mourning. It also records a unique cosmological sign during the time of Prophet David (peace be upon him), where wild beasts observed fasting, illustrating the interconnectedness of creation with prophetic spiritual states.
